settle: Wind and local rain are the main untested rivals for the tide effect (the other-ZIP set also rises, 1.15 per 10 cm, and contains waterfront ZIPs); a Jamaica Bay or Rockaway gauge, hourly local rain and event-level matching with FloodNet would separate them. For the trend, more years: 16 annual counts cannot separate 0.55 days/yr/yr from zero.

notes:
Held-out sample: 1882 dry days in 2010-2019 (Sandy window 29 Oct to 30 Nov 2012 dropped), 173 with maximum at or above 0.35 m MHHW, 2042 C3 complaints in the 8 coastal ZIPs and 28899 in the other ZIPs; minimum-data rule met. Only 7 dry days reached the NOS minor level (0.563 m), so the first claim's threshold could not be used. Registered 311 queries were run with agency = 'DEP' added and in one-year chunks because the unrestricted upper() LIKE query timed out; all matching records in 2010-2019 for the case-sensitive patterns belong to DEP (249,360 records including sewer backups). Checks, tidal rate ratio per 10 cm: knot 0.30 1.73, 0.40 2.38, 0.45 2.88; street flooding only 3.02 (2.36 to 4.22); with sewer backups 1.53; log-linear over all dry days 1.11 (1.06 to 1.15); 2020-2025 in-sample 2.13; shifted-tide placebos 0.99 and 0.97. The registered shape was flat below the knot, but the band model shows the complaint rate already above the reference in 0.30 to 0.35 m (rate ratio 1.34), so the rise is smooth, not a threshold. Part 2a: annual counts 2010-2025 range from 11 to 41 (2024); detrending the tide by 2.95 mm/yr gives a slope of 0.01 (-0.79 to 0.81); the gauge's own annual-mean slope over 2010-2025 is 4.0 mm/yr, above the long-term 2.95. The verdict is decided by part 1 alone as registered.

After the referee (13 Nov 2026): the referee reproduced the result with an independent bootstrap (2.00, 1.64 to 2.34) and it survives stricter dry-day rules, wind, season and influence checks. Three qualifications are added. The figure of 2.00 per 10 cm depends on the knot (1.73, 2.00, 2.38 and 2.88 at 0.30 to 0.45 m; 1.11 per 10 cm log-linear over all dry days) and should not be quoted as a general dose-response; the direction and the coastal specificity do not depend on it. The effect is concentrated in the Rockaway ZIP codes (2.01 to 2.52); Howard Beach, which supplies 625 of the 2,042 complaints, shows 1.25 (0.98 to 1.59) and Red Hook 1.10 (0.70 to 1.73). Several of the busiest dry days follow Hurricane Irene, and without the ten busiest days the estimate is 1.82 (1.60 to 2.17). The other-ZIP series also rises, so some common factor moves complaints citywide on high-water days. The referee added the strongest evidence against the weather rival: complaints in the coastal set follow the part of the water level that is predictable from lunar and seasonal periods (1.083 per 10 cm, SE 0.020) as well as the remainder (1.136, SE 0.022). In data/derived/round2/tidal_trend/graph_flood_findings.json the records under 'flooding -> post-traumatic stress disorder' with PMIDs 29344631, 32758312 and 24368465 are trials of a psychotherapy technique called flooding and are not flood evidence; docs/round2.md already says that the concept 'flooding' is mis-grounded, and no outcome cites those records.
verdict_note: Direction and coastal specificity are confirmed. The size (2.00 per 10 cm) depends on the knot and the effect is concentrated in the Rockaway ZIP codes.
